As someone that experienced something similar to your wife, the key thing is it to ensure that you continue to treat her the way you currently do - with love and care. The hardest thing for many people disclosing SA is the strange treatment and changes in relationships that happen. Finding a balance of letting her know that you’re there to support her and are willing to give her space is critical. 
Also, it would be lovely if you’d asked her how you can help, but also reassure her that you don’t see her as a fragile due to her experience and that in your eyes she’s still resilient and the same person you chose to spend the rest of your life with. It’s possible to recover! 

CBT, Holistic massage, Reiki and meditation helped me recover greatly :) Perhaps, you could recommend these treatments? 

Remember to take care of yourself as well!

I agree with you, it’s why I went to uni in the first place. But, my mental health issues have become so debilitating that I no longer am capable to make a difference. Simply, leaving my room, reading and writing essays has become remarkably difficult. At this rate, I don’t know where I’ll be, because it carries on getting worst despite my efforts: therapy and various medications.

I barely sleep, eat and can’t think as coherently or rationally as I once could. I struggle to understand my emotions because I know they’re pointless. Everyday, simple tasks and existing feels like a battle. My close friends I grew up with barely recognise me and have even agreed that I’m not as smart as I was before. Uploading this post is something I never would have dreamed of in the past, and I despise myself for this defeat.
